from.place: the constructible variant clause and its bounded flat constructible model

title: Etale bounded flat constructible model
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, let X be a Noetherian scheme, and let a b : ℤ with an explicit hypothesis hab : a ≤ b. For every bounded constructible object K of the derived category of sheaves of Λ-modules on the small etale site of X, K has Tor amplitude in [a,b] if and only if there exists a cochain complex P of such sheaves that is flat and constructible termwise, zero outside [a,b], and whose image in the derived category is isomorphic to K. The site and sheaf categories use [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and Tor amplitude is the derived-category Tor-amplitude notion in the cited declaration. Here bounded constructible means $H^n(K)=0$ for all but finitely many $n$, with each $H^n(K)$ constructible in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. The derived category and its localization $Q$ are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ means $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F[0])=0$ for every sheaf $F$ and every $i<a$ or $i>b$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude; def-kun-derived-tensor]. Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact; zero outside $[a,b]$ means every such term is a zero object. All sheaves use the ModuleCat encoding of $\Lambda$-module sheaves.

proof.text: Convert the given bounded finite-value-constructible hypothesis to the source boundedConstructible predicate. Its integer cohomology bounds give the canonical t-structure IsGE and IsLE conditions by DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] to every cohomology sheaf. This gives exactly the hypothesis of the already-proved source theorem hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel.

For the forward implication, apply the forward direction of the existing source theorem hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel. Its proof implements the planned construction: the source constructibility class is closed under kernels and cokernels by [thm-constructible-serre]; its flat subclass contains zero and is stable under isomorphisms and binary biproducts, the latter using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct]. The lifting theorem [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible-lifting] supplies the class-resolution hypothesis, and [lem-sf-flat-model-class-resolution] gives the bounded flat constructible model by lower good truncation. Thus the existing source theorem packages these four stated dependencies, without bypassing the unit construction.

Unpack IsBoundedFlatComplex into support outside [a,b] and termwise flatness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] in reverse to each model term. Reverse the source isomorphism K ≅ Q(P) to obtain Q(P) ≅ K. These are exactly the four clauses requested for the model.

Conversely, discard only termwise constructibility. Pair the given support and flatness into IsBoundedFlatComplex, reverse Q(P) ≅ K, and apply the reverse implication of [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] with the converted bounded-constructible hypothesis. This proves the original Tor amplitude predicate in the same interval.
